newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: OUTPUT RESTARTS AT COLOMBIA'S CANO LIMON FIELD.
newsitem.headline: OUTPUT RESTARTS AT COLOMBIA'S CANO LIMON FIELD.

text.p: Hydrocarbon production has restarted in the Cano Limon oil field in northeast Colombia almost a week after it was shut in following a wave of leftist rebel attacks, field operator Occidental Petroleum Corp said.
A spokesman for the U.S. multinational said the force majeure which was declared on production on Aug. 4 could also be lifted Monday.
Engineers from the state-run oil company Ecopetrol finished repairing the crippled pipeline that pumps crude from Cano Limon to the Caribbean coast lifting terminal at Covenas late Saturday.

The Occidental spokesman said the field was now producing at a rate of 175,000 barrels per day and that the pipeline was pumping about 230,000 barrels per day, including some of the 500,000 barrels of crude held in on-site storage tanks.

"We're once again producing in Cano Limon. Production restarted as soon as the pipeline was repaired," the spokesman said. "I suppose, but cannot confirm categorically, that force majeure in the field will be lifted today."

The pipeline has been out of action since July 30 after a rebel dynamite attack. It was then bombed twice more and partially destroyed by a landslide in the next four days. Ecopetrol has not yet said when force majeure on crude exports could be lifted.
